attempts.purpose: entity_type/field-id mismatch to reproduce the preprod 400-error-shape finding
attempts.produced: {success:false, error:'Something went wrong'} -- error is a plain STRING, not the declared object schema {code,message,details}. Field 233776 is a TestCase-scoped field; passing it under entity_type=test-result reproduces the declared entity_type/field mismatch case.

item_shape.variant_match: NEITHER variant A (field-definition: {value,name,internal_name,is_default}) NOR variant B (case-row: {id,internal_name,field_name,colour,value_category,name}). This is a THIRD, distinct shape -- a dataset-option-row keyed by option_value/dataset_id/record_status, closely mirroring the option_values sub-objects returned inline by get_project_id_custom_fields_v2_v1 (option_value, is_default, record_status, created_at, updated_at, dataset_id) but with extra relational keys (id, group_id, project_id, custom_field_id, parent_option_id) not present there either.

undeclared_returned: values[].id, group_id, project_id, custom_field_id, dataset_id, option_value, is_default, parent_option_id, record_status, created_at, updated_at -- ALL undeclared, since the capability's own schema types `values[]` items as a bare `object` with no listed properties. Not a contract violation (nothing was promised to be absent), but confirms the item shape was genuinely unspecified until this probe.

prod_vs_preprod.point_1_declared_contract: Matches preprod exactly: dynamic top-level key '<field_id>': {field_type, values}, plus info and success. Declared 400 schema is the structured object {success:false, error:{code,message,details}}.

point_2_nonempty_values_found.note: Unlike preprod (every field tried had values:[]), project 332537's real custom dropdown fields have plenty of configured option values, letting the item shape and duplicate/paging checks actually run.

prod_vs_preprod.point_3_item_shape: Third/distinct shape (see probe.item_shape above) -- neither declared variant A nor B from preprod's hypothesis; a dataset-option-row with id/group_id/project_id/custom_field_id/dataset_id/option_value/is_default/parent_option_id/record_status/created_at/updated_at.

point_4_duplicate_option_ids.detail: Across all values inspected for field 233776 (33/33, both pages) and field 180001 (90 of 120 rows inspected across pages 1, 2 and 4, plus targeted q= searches), every option_value string was unique -- no organic duplicate names and no systematic doubling of a 'default' option. Also, every single option row in this project's custom dropdown/multi_dropdown fields carries is_default:false (per get_project_id_custom_fields_v2_v1) -- unlike preprod's SYSTEM field defaults (status/priority/etc.), this project has no custom-field option flagged as the canonical default at all, so the preprod 'default option cloned twice' pattern has no equivalent case to even test here. Distinguish from get_system_field_values_v1's prod findings (that capability's SYSTEM fields had real organic duplicate names, e.g. 'Temp state' x5) -- this capability's CUSTOM fields, on the same project, showed none in the sampled rows.

point_5_400_error_shape.detail: Entity_type/field-id mismatch (field_id=233776, a test-case field, requested under entity_type=test-result) returned HTTP 400 with body {success:false, error:'Something went wrong'} -- error is a plain STRING. This exactly reproduces the preprod DRIFT: contradicts the declared object schema {code,message,details}, matches the capability's own prose guidance ('A field that does not exist, or any upstream failure, returns 400 {success:false, error:'Something went wrong''), and matches prod's own get_system_field_values_v1-adjacent pattern of string-shaped errors.

point_6_paging_reliability.detail: Checked non-final and final pages on two fields with real data: field 233776 (count=33, page_size=30) -- page 1 returned exactly 30/30 rows (full, next=2), page 2 (final, next=null) returned exactly 3/3 rows (30+3=33, matches declared count exactly). Field 180001 (count=120, page_size=30) -- page 1 returned 30/30 (next=2), page 2 (non-final, next=3) returned 30/30, page 4 (final, next=null) returned 30/30 (4*30=120, matches declared count exactly). q-filtered checks also agreed: q='Chiranjeevi' declared count=1, returned 1 row (next=null); q='d1' declared count=12, returned 12 rows (next=null). In every case checked on prod, info.count and info.page_size were fully consistent with actual rows returned -- this capability's paging/filtering metadata does NOT reproduce the under-fill / undercount bug seen on get_system_field_values_v1. This is a genuine positive distinction worth recording: the two capabilities share a similar info{page,page_size,count,prev,next} shape but do not share the same paging-metadata reliability defect on this data.

notes: Verdict is DRIFT and reproduces_preprod=true, driven entirely by point 5: the declared 400 error schema is a structured object {code,message,details}, but the actual body for an entity_type/field-id mismatch is {success:false, error:'Something went wrong'} with error as a plain string -- confirmed again on production with real data, exactly as found on preprod. Point 2 is now settled (previously UNVERIFIED on preprod): production project 332537 has multiple custom dropdown fields with genuinely configured, non-empty option values, so this recheck was able to observe the item shape for real. Point 3 is a new finding: the value/option item shape is a THIRD distinct shape (dataset-option-row: id/group_id/project_id/custom_field_id/dataset_id/option_value/is_default/parent_option_id/record_status/created_at/updated_at), not either of the two hypothesized variants (A: field-definition, B: case-row) -- and since the capability's own declared schema types `values[]` items as a bare, property-less object, this is new information rather than a contract violation. Point 4 (duplicate-option-id check) found no duplicates and, notably, no custom-field option anywhere flagged is_default:true in this project, so the preprod 'default dropdown cloned twice' pattern (which was specific to SYSTEM fields on get_system_field_values_v1) has no analogous case to reproduce or refute here -- reported as 'not applicable to this data' rather than forced into a pass/fail. Point 6 is a genuine POSITIVE distinction from get_system_field_values_v1: paging metadata (info.count/page_size vs actual rows returned) was fully self-consistent across every page and every q-filtered call checked here, on both a 33-row and a 120-row field, unfiltered and filtered, final and non-final pages -- the sibling capability's under-fill/undercount defect does not reproduce on get_custom_field_values_v1 with this data. Limitation: list_workspace_fields_v2 returned a systemic 403 'This action is not permitted for the user' (SSO/auth block, confirmed with and without query params) in this environment, so real field ids for entity_type test-result / test-plan / exploratory-session could not be enumerated live; get_project_id_custom_fields_v2_v1 only ever serves TestCase fields by its own declared design, so no alternate live path existed within probe budget. The entity_type-mismatch 400 check (point 5) was still exercised successfully using a real TestCase field id requested under entity_type=test-result, which is sufficient to trigger and confirm the mismatch-error-shape behavior, but a genuine non-empty test-result/test-plan/exploratory-session custom field's item shape remains UNVERIFIED on prod.
